entries.steps: Client settings → Cache → Cache capacity. Maximum space Delight can use for cached files.
Client settings → Cache → Clear cache. Remove cached files. Delight will fetch them again as needed.
Client settings → Cosmetics → Delight Cosmetics. Install and maintain Delight capes for supported Fabric 1.21.11 instances.
Client settings → General → Startup Behavior. Choose what happens when Delight Client starts. Choices include Open Home, Open Settings, Remember last page.
Client settings → General → Minimize to System Tray. Close button will minimize Delight Client to your system tray.
Client settings → General → Right Sidebar. Choose what to show beside the main workspace.
Client settings → Appearance → Color mode. Choose how the launcher looks.
Client settings → Appearance → Accent. The highlight color for buttons, selections and active controls. Choices include Custom.
Client settings → Appearance → Dividers. Adjust the visibility of lines between sections and rows.
Client settings → Appearance → Font. Choose the typeface for launcher menus and controls.
Client settings → Appearance → Interface size. Adjust the size of text and controls.
Client settings → Appearance → Spacing. Choose how much room the interface uses.
Client settings → Appearance → Reduce motion. Use fewer animations throughout the launcher.
Client settings → Appearance → Button Pop Duration. Choose how quickly buttons press and spring back. Set to 0 for no button pop.
Client settings → Performance → Ultra Performance Mode. Disable motion, glow, blur, and continuous visual rendering for lower-end computers.
Client settings → Performance → Memory Allocation. Set how much RAM Minecraft can use. Choices include 2048 MB, 4096 MB, 6144 MB, 8192 MB.
Client settings → Performance → Java Runtime. Automatic detects or securely installs the exact Java Minecraft needs.
Client settings → Performance → Delight-managed Java. Delight installs private runtimes automatically when needed. Your system Java and PATH stay the same.
Client settings → Performance → Java Arguments. Advanced JVM arguments for Minecraft launches.
Client settings → Minecraft → Default Game Version. Used when creating a new instance. Choices include Latest release.
Client settings → Minecraft → Default Mod Loader. The loader selected for new instances. Choices include Fabric, Vanilla.
Client settings → Launcher → Home Layout. Choose between Delight's full dashboard and a focused traditional launcher. Choices include Dashboard, Spotlight.
Client settings → Launcher → Double Click to Play. Quickly double-click an instance to launch it. A single click still opens its page.
Client settings → Launcher → Launch Method. Choose how Minecraft windows open. Choices include Standard window, Fullscreen.
Client settings → Launcher → Close Launcher After Launch. Automatically close Delight Client after Minecraft starts.
Client settings → Downloads → Download Queue. Choose how many downloads can run at once. Choices include 1 simultaneous download, 3 simultaneous downloads, 5 simultaneous downloads.
Client settings → Privacy → Usage Analytics. Store anonymous feature-use counters locally on this device.
Client settings → Privacy → Crash Reports. Save crash details locally so they can be reviewed in Logs.
Client settings → Privacy → News and Recommendations. Show relevant client updates on Home. Choices include Show recommendations, Hide recommendations.
Client settings → Updates → Automatic Checks. Check GitHub Releases once whenever Delight Client opens.
Client settings → Updates → Current Version. The version currently installed on this computer.
Client settings → Advanced → Debug Logging. Write more detailed logs for troubleshooting.
Client settings → Advanced → Game Directory. Choose where Minecraft files and instances are stored.
Client settings → Advanced → Onboarding. Run the Microsoft setup again.
Client settings → Advanced → Minecraft Account. Remove the saved Microsoft account from this device.
Client settings → Advanced → Reset Preferences. Return Delight Client settings to their defaults.
Open an instance → Instance name. The name shown in your instance list and on Home.

Open an instance → Minecraft memory. The maximum RAM Minecraft can use for this instance. Larger modpacks may need more. Leave enough RAM for your system and other apps; allocating more does not always improve performance.

Open an instance → Java profile. Default uses launcher-managed Java settings. Performance uses conservative garbage-collection tuning. Overdrive is experimental and may use more memory or fail with incompatible Java versions. FPS gains are not guaranteed. Custom opens the argument editor.

Open an instance → JVM arguments. Extra flags passed to Java when this instance launches. Choosing a profile replaces these flags. Invalid or conflicting arguments can prevent launch. Reset to default clears the custom flags. Save changes applies your edits.

Utilities → Sync Across Instances → Game Settings. Copy Minecraft settings, including controls, video, and sound, from the selected instance to every other instance. This replaces their game settings. Choose Off to leave them alone.
Utilities → Sync Across Instances → Saved Servers. Copy the selected instance’s multiplayer server list to every other instance. This replaces each destination’s list rather than combining lists.

Utilities → Sync Across Instances → Voice Chat Settings. Copy Simple Voice Chat client settings from the chosen instance to only the instances you select below. This does not install the voice chat mod.

Utilities → Sync Across Instances → Shared Resource Packs. Connect every instance to one resource-pack folder. Packs are available everywhere, but each instance still chooses which ones to enable. Changes to the shared files affect all connected instances.

Utilities → Sync Across Instances → Shared Shader Packs. Connect every instance to one shader-pack folder. Each instance still needs a compatible shader mod and chooses its own active shader. Changes to the shared files affect all connected instances.

Utilities → saving and syncing. Save setup remembers your choices without changing game files or the active sync rules. Sync now applies and activates these choices. Changed files are backed up first.

Instance settings → Fabric Loader version. Choose the loader used on the next launch, then save changes. This changes Fabric Loader, not Minecraft or Fabric API. Your mods may require a particular loader version.
Client settings → Appearance → Theme preset. Save or apply a group of appearance settings.
